question: Which artist has the most tracks in the catalogue?

query: WITH track_counts AS ( SELECT a.artist_id, -- group per artist ar.name AS artist_name, COUNT(t.track_id) AS track_count FROM chinook.track AS t JOIN chinook.album AS a ON a.album_id = t.album_id -- map track to its album JOIN chinook.artist AS ar ON ar.artist_id = a.artist_id -- map album to its artist GROUP BY a.artist_id, ar.name ), ranked AS ( SELECT artist_name, track_count, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY track_count DESC) AS rnk -- highest counts get rank 1 (ties allowed) FROM track_counts ) SELECT artist_name, track_count FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1 -- keep artist(s) with the most tracks ORDER BY artist_name; -- stable order if there is a tie

question: Which customers bought music in more than one genre?
answer:
I pulled customers with purchases spanning more than one genre and ranked them by the number of distinct genres they bought.

What I did:
- Joined invoices -> invoice_line -> track -> genre to identify each customer’s purchased genres.
- Counted distinct genres per customer and filtered for those with more than one.
- Returned the top 20 by distinct-genre count.

Highlights (units: count of distinct genres; all-time across the dataset):
- Customer 57 (Luis Rojas): 12 genres — Alternative & Punk, Blues, Classical, Drama, Easy Listening, Latin, Metal, Rock, Sci Fi & Fantasy, Science Fiction, Soundtrack, TV Shows
- Customer 45 (Ladislav Kovács): 11 genres — Alternative & Punk, Blues, Comedy, Drama, Electronica/Dance, Latin, Metal, R&B/Soul, Rock, Sci Fi & Fantasy, TV Shows
- Customer 34 (João Fernandes): 10 genres — Alternative & Punk, Electronica/Dance, Latin, Metal, Pop, R&B/Soul, Rock, Sci Fi & Fantasy, TV Shows, World
- Customer 14 (Mark Philips): 10 genres — Alternative & Punk, Blues, Bossa Nova, Electronica/Dance, Jazz, Latin, Metal, R&B/Soul, Rock, World
- Customer 24 (Frank Ralston): 10 genres — Alternative, Alternative & Punk, Classical, Comedy, Hip Hop/Rap, Latin, Metal, R&B/Soul, Rock, TV Shows

I’ve charted the top 20 customers by number of genres purchased so you can quickly see who buys most broadly. Want me to list all such customers instead of the top 20?
query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.genre_id) AS genre_count, -- number of distinct genres purchased STRING_AGG(DISTINCT g.name, ', ' ORDER BY g.name) AS genres -- list of genres purchased FROM chinook.customer AS c JOIN chinook.invoice AS i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN chinook.invoice_line AS il ON il.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN chinook.track AS t ON t.track_id = il.track_id JOIN chinook.genre AS g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE t.genre_id IS NOT NULL -- exclude tracks without a genre to avoid inflating counts GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.genre_id) > 1 -- more than one genre purchased ORDER BY genre_count DESC, c.last_name, c.first_name LIMIT 20;

question: What share of revenue comes from the top 5 customers?
answer: The top 5 customers account for 10.10% of all-time revenue, contributing $235.10 out of a total $2,328.60 (USD), based on invoice totals across all invoices in the database.
query: WITH customer_rev AS ( SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, SUM(i.total) AS revenue_usd -- sum of invoice totals per customer (USD) FROM chinook.invoice i JOIN chinook.customer c ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id -- link invoices to customers WHERE i.total IS NOT NULL -- ignore any null totals GROUP BY c.customer_id, customer_name ), total_rev AS ( SELECT SUM(revenue_usd) AS total_revenue_usd FROM customer_rev -- total revenue across all customers ), top5 AS ( SELECT customer_id, customer_name, revenue_usd FROM customer_rev ORDER BY revenue_usd DESC -- highest revenue first LIMIT 5 -- top 5 customers ), top5_sum AS ( SELECT SUM(revenue_usd) AS top5_revenue_usd FROM top5 -- sum revenue of top 5 customers ) SELECT ROUND((t5.top5_revenue_usd / tr.total_revenue_usd) * 100.0, 2) AS top5_share_percent, -- share as percentage of total ROUND(t5.top5_revenue_usd::numeric, 2) AS top5_revenue_usd, -- USD ROUND(tr.total_revenue_usd::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue_usd -- USD FROM top5_sum t5 CROSS JOIN total_rev tr;

Here are the top genres by tracks sold (units = individual tracks, all time). I ranked them descending and returned the top 20.

- Rock — 835
- Latin — 386
- Metal — 264
- Alternative & Punk — 258
- Jazz — 205
- TV Shows — 186
- Blues — 164
- Drama — 157
- R&B/Soul — 152
- Hip Hop/Rap — 145
- Electronica/Dance — 144
- Pop — 105
- Easy Listening — 103
- Classical — 102
- Alternative — 96
- Heavy Metal — 83
- Comedy — 77
- Soundtrack — 74

Interpretation: Rock is the clear leader by track units sold, with roughly double the next genre (Latin). If you want this broken down by year or country, I can slice it further.
query: -- Top genres by tracks sold (all time) SELECT g.name AS genre, SUM(il.quantity) AS tracks_sold FROM chinook.invoice_line AS il JOIN chinook.track AS t ON t.track_id = il.track_id -- link sold items to tracks JOIN chinook.genre AS g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id -- get track genre WHERE t.genre_id IS NOT NULL -- exclude tracks without a genre to avoid NULL group AND g.name IS NOT NULL -- exclude NULL genre names GROUP BY g.name ORDER BY tracks_sold DESC, genre ASC LIMIT 20;
